reason: I'll start with the after-meal situation: the picture says higher blood glucose prompts insulin release, which should help muscle store glucose.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release insulin; I'm not sure exactly how the game will show it.

alternatives.reason: The lower-glucose route also matches a goal, but I'd rather follow the after-meal sequence first.

effect: Insulin entered the blood as expected, so I can follow its route to the muscle.
reaction: The picture makes the chemical message's destination clear.
reason: I'll continue the after-meal sequence by bringing insulin to the muscle fibres, where glucose is already available.
expectation: I expect the muscle to take in glucose and store some of it, though I'm not sure how the result will show that.

alternatives.reason: I also need to explore the lower-glucose message, but I want to finish the insulin route first.

effect: The muscle stored glucose while insulin stayed outside, completing the after-meal goal. I'll follow the lower-glucose route next.
reaction: It helps to see that insulin is a message rather than part of the store.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it starts the remaining goal for the between-meals message.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release the other hormone into the blood; I don't yet know its name.

effect: The lower-glucose signal released a hormone carried to the liver, so I can now follow its effect on the store.
reaction: The label makes the hormone's purpose clear, though it doesn't give its name.
reason: This is the only offered combination and matches the remaining goal of releasing stored liver glucose.
expectation: I expect the liver to break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver store released glucose into the blood as expected, and the chapter is complete. The result also says the release signal eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: The shrinking store made the between-meals route easy to picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to the muscle was most worthwhile: it showed glucose becoming a store while insulin stayed outside as a message.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing the second hormone was a little less engaging because its label explained its destination and the next combination was the only one offered.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the picture to make such a clear distinction between insulin as a message and glucose as the material stored.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the last two combinations were guided by the goal and the only available options rather than choices I figured out independently.

continue.text: I would probably continue: comparing the muscle's storage route with the liver's release route made the two situations understandable, even though the choices became limited.
